description: We are a group of students coming from various backgrounds to build a project that is impactful and engaging to our users.
summary:
What good is a discovery if your spacecraft can’t send it home? Moonbound, a browser game by Miners in Space, puts students in charge of a science mission. Players can look for wildfires from Earth orbit, scout the Moon’s south pole for clues to water ice, or study Neptune’s atmosphere with an orbiter and a descent probe.

Players assemble a spacecraft room by room, choose instruments within mass, power, and budget limits, and run a launch readiness check. After liftoff, they enter the ship they built and operate its equipment. During a radiation warning, for example, they switch off the camera while keeping the flight computer running. In Lunar Ice Scout, inspired by NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, players learn why a hydrogen reading calls for follow-up measurements before they can conclude there’s water ice.

Moonbound answers the NASA Space Apps Space Mission Design Game challenge by connecting design decisions to what players can do in flight and what science they can send home. Players can revise their designs and fly again to test a different approach.
details:
For our project, we had two different approaches. One was through Godot, and one was through React + vite. We wanted to see how our game would look with each approach. We used the assistance of AI to vibe code our web app game as a proof of concept. However we also used Godot to try and achieve that vision. It was a new tool for the whole team so development was slow.

In our slideshow you can see both of the approaches. We plan to finish this game with Godot in the future. We hope that this game gets future astronauts interested in space.
